headline: Law Student Celebrates 'Legal Independence' By Representing His Own Cat in Housing Dispute
body:
Following the recent judicial clarification that the Bar Council has no authority to penalize law students, 23-year-old final-year student Aarav Mehta has immediately pivoted to a lucrative private practice representing his tabby cat, 'Billo,' in a high-stakes litigation against the household's Roomba.

"The ruling was a green light for all of us," said Mehta, while adjusting his makeshift black robe fashioned from a discarded velvet curtain. "Without the BCI peering over my shoulder to check if I’m 'behaving' like a student, I decided that my first client should be someone who truly understands the concept of absolute, unearned arrogance. Billo has already drafted a 40-page memorandum on why the vacuum cleaner is a psychological aggressor that violates his basic right to nap in the hallway."

Local legal experts note that Mehta has spent the last 48 hours filing motions to his own refrigerator and serving subpoenas to the neighbor’s Golden Retriever. "He’s finally free to practice the kind of law that actually matters," said his roommate, who is currently being sued for ‘unjust enrichment’ regarding the last packet of Maggi noodles. "He’s moved from studying the IPC to studying the specific local bylaws of cat-nip procurement and territorial floor rights."

Mehta maintains that as long as he isn’t officially a member of the Bar, he is technically a 'freelance jurisprudential consultant' for the feline community. "I’m not practicing law without a license," he clarified, while preparing to cross-examine a stray pigeon on the balcony. "I’m practicing the art of being a nuisance, which is the foundational pillar of the entire legal system anyway."
caption: Law student finally realizes that if you can't be disciplined, you might as well sue the blender. 🐱⚖️ #LawStudent #LegalHumor #CatLaw #SupremeCourt (satire)
